---
name: mdcw-national-trees
description: Design, extend, implement, or review national focus trees for Enes's HOI4 Millennium Dawn Cold War mod, using the project's historical, political, reward, and native MD presentation conventions. Use for national focus content, not research trees or unrelated main-Imperia changes.
---

# MD Cold War national trees

Build a playable national programme for the January 1970 multiplayer roleplay scenario. Follow current MD mechanics and presentation while preserving approved Imperia and Cold War features. A matching name or tooltip is not proof that a reward works.

Read [project-contract.md](references/project-contract.md) for the user's durable preferences and their scope. Read [source-map.md](references/source-map.md) to locate the code and chat evidence. Reconfirm mutable facts in the target checkout; snapshots are not permanent instructions.

## Establish the assignment

- Identify country, scenario, existing tree, source generator, requested phase, and any approved design. Distinguish national focus trees from research trees.
- Preserve historical starting leaders and existing election, succession, economic, diplomatic, and party systems unless the task changes them. Add content through those systems.
- For a new tree, prepare the spatial design and effects first. If the user requests a sketch or explicitly reserves approval, keep it outside the loaded mod until approval arrives. When implementation of a concrete design is authorized, proceed without asking for the same permission again. A layout-only fix does not authorize changing rewards or prerequisites.
- Inspect current work and generator ownership before editing shared files. Assign non-overlapping agent work; do not run a broad generator that can overwrite another chat's changes.

## Learn the actual reference grammar

Use the normal main MD 2000-era national trees as references for values, costs, modifiers, reward bundles, native code and presentation. The reference pool includes Russia, Israel, Germany and Turkey, plus other mechanically comparable countries; select the examples that fit the effect being built. Read [russia-2000-presentation.md](references/russia-2000-presentation.md) for the concrete mistakes learned from Iraq and the verified examples. Compare representative descriptions, English localisation and actual reward code when authoring or substantially rewriting content. For numerical calibration, record the source country/focus, amount, unit, cost, duration and relevant gates. Adapt the scale to the target country and 1970 scenario; these are mechanical references, not political or historical templates. The custom Soviet 1970 tree remains an architecture/gameplay reference.

The lesson is to deliver finished MD-quality content: descriptions explain this country's circumstances, institutions, political intent and meaningful tensions; effects clearly show the actual named outcomes, numbers, costs and trade-offs using native MD presentation. Do not publish raw catalogue instructions (such as "Pay for a factory"), generic filler, placeholder summaries, internal bookkeeping essays, or prose substitutes for executable/numeric effects. Merely deleting technical words, lengthening a description, citing a reference tree, or passing a parser is not an editorial/presentation review. Treat concept-catalogue text as a draft even when its mechanics are approved. Read the emitted descriptions and reward lists together before delivery; for substantial new or rewritten content, have an independent agent compare representative examples against main MD. Preserve approved calculations, guarded transactions and the country-specific design.

Read comparable branches in current main MD `00_generic.txt`, `05_russia.txt`, `05_israel.txt`, `05_germany.txt` and `turkey.txt` as relevant, alongside the target country's native tree. An individual task does not require exhaustively reading every tree. Trace their called effects, ideas, dynamic modifiers and UI rather than copying only focus declarations. Project generators are integration examples, not proof that every local line is correct.

The user also selected Claude's implemented Soviet 1970 tree as a preferred project reference for programme depth, thematic reward bundles, leadership variation and integration. Read [soviet-patterns.md](references/soviet-patterns.md) when designing large programmes, leader paths, decisions or cooperative focuses. Adapt its architecture, not Soviet-only institutions, values or focus count.

Record a small reference profile: source/version, focus cost and duration, entry/branch/join coordinates, icon treatment, party gates, reward shapes and units. Sample comparable political, industrial, military and diplomatic focuses. A superpower's factory grant is not automatically a small country's reward budget.

## Design policy choices, not a chain of small gifts

- Research January 1970 institutions, parties, conflicts, economy and constraints. Cite primary historical sources where possible. Separate historical facts, plausible alternate history and balance proposals.
- Build historical and credible alternative routes for relevant parties, outlooks and leaders. Do not fill every MD slot with an implausible country path. Preserve playable continuation for approved alternatives.
- Use MD's exact party/subparty model. A programme becomes available when that party governs; do not require a redundant 'unlock our already-ruling party' focus. Accession focuses are justified when they really change government through the agreed system. Show an unapproved new party as a provisional design; do not invent a live ideology or party-array slot to make it fit.
- Give important programmes meaningful outcomes: appropriate buildings, sector productivity/employment, debt or treasury consequences, programme modifiers, research/doctrine rewards, diplomacy or decisions. Avoid PP/stability filler unrelated to the focus's purpose.
- Make both sides of a historically grounded exclusive choice attractive: the player should want both rewards but have a real reason to choose. Give them different substantial outcomes and, where plausible, a modest disadvantage or credible opportunity cost. Strengthen existing forks before multiplying cosmetic exclusions. Exclude competing constitutional terms, scarce funding priorities or military commitments; keep ordinary complementary development shared. A difficult historical situation and its starting penalties remain real; this preference is not a mandate to make every policy harmless.
- Audit impact across a whole compatible route, including its follow-ups, starting spirits, temporary decisions and government gates. Do not sum incompatible parties or add several versions of the same army reform on top of one another. Replace overlapping rewards explicitly. Prefer meaningful assets, limited-use research/doctrine bonuses, training and enacted institutions to repetitive tiny PP/stability changes or bureaucracy-only penalties. Check whether a positive reward is already lost at an existing cap.
- Give important choices enough distinct follow-through to change the programme. Merge accounting/review filler into the reform it serves; avoid stamping every party with the same focus count, doubled fork and ceremonial finale. These are outcome criteria, not a universal minimum bonus, mandatory malus or prescribed number of forks.
- Include relevant starting problems and ways to improve them. Reforms should change an actual persistent system, not just rename a spirit.
- Avoid arbitrary date barriers. Retain dates where historically or mechanically necessary and explain them; a chapter name alone does not justify locking an entire programme until that year.

## Use one reviewable design

Maintain structured design data where a generator exists. Each focus needs an ID, English name/description, group, coordinates/anchor, prerequisite groups, exclusions, availability, cost, executable effects, associated sprites/ideas/events and its MD reference pattern. Mark one-time, temporary, recurring or party-bound effects explicitly.

Produce a full-tree preview with existing neighbours and normal-scale branch views, using the same resolved coordinates, connectors and labels as the proposed code. A focus inspector should expose conditions and exact proposed rewards. Narrative prose belongs in descriptions; normal completion rewards remain in native tooltips.

Use `$mdcw-tree-layout` for substantial geometry work and `$mdcw-modifier-audit` for mechanics/reference verification when available. They are installed alongside this skill; the requirements below still apply if either is unavailable.

## Implement and prove the integration

For approved-concept implementation, native succession, government-bound programmes or difficult economic starts, read [vietnam-integration.md](references/vietnam-integration.md). It records the Vietnam implementation lessons without turning its roster, reward counts or dates into requirements for other countries.

1. Edit the canonical generator/design and intended outputs. Match nearby MD blocks and scopes. Use searchable `COLDWAR_<TAG>_...` IDs unless an established country namespace exists; preserve existing IDs/save contracts.
2. Trace each promised effect to its provider and consumer. Check amount, scope, timing, stacking, affordability and displayed units. Helper names alone do not establish behaviour.
3. Preserve prerequisite grouping and gameplay choices while positioning: separate `prerequisite` blocks are AND; multiple `focus` entries inside one block are OR. Do not silently convert visible dependencies into invisible eligibility gates just to simplify lines.
4. Implement appropriate removal, replacement or conditional deactivation on government changes and expiration. Distinguish durable national gains from currently active party/leader programmes; preserve earned programme variables if later reactivation is intended. Resynchronization must not replay factories, cash, annexations or research grants.
5. Register English localisation, sprites/textures, ideas/modifiers/events and transitive dependencies. Reuse appropriate art before creating new art. Do not alter global fonts or other trees to accommodate one branch.
6. Delegate a layout review and independent mechanics/reference review for substantial work, using the user's preferred economical model when available. Review emitted code, not only the catalogue. Keep implementation and final review independent where practical.
7. Run applicable checks and visually inspect the faithful preview. Test in HOI4 when available: new 1970 start, hover/tooltips, representative rewards, party change, save/reload, AI and multiplayer responses as relevant. Report unperformed engine checks plainly.

## Deliver

Explain branches/choices added, important effects/costs, files touched, verification and remaining gaps. Separate designed, implemented, statically checked, visually reviewed and tested in HOI4. Disclose deviations from the approved design. Do not claim perfection or working modifiers merely because parsing passed. Skill invocation does not authorize publication or unrelated system changes.

# Project contract learned from the user's requests

Maintained authoring preferences, not blanket authorization. The current request wins. Keep country-specific choices country-specific; research-tree corrections are not national-focus geometry rules.

## Recurring requirements

| Concern | Apply this decision |
|---|---|
| Target | January 1970 Cold War multiplayer roleplay. Main MD/Imperia is a separate product; its individual audit decisions do not automatically apply here. |
| Base | Current MD architecture and supported APIs; preserve approved Cold War/Imperia additions and balance. |
| Language | All new in-game text in English. Communicate with Enes in German unless asked otherwise. |
| Design | Full spatial tree and effects first. A list is not a tree visualization. Respect an explicit approval boundary. |
| Look | Native MD grammar, especially Generic/Russia 2000 and applicable Germany party branches. No invented font, giant gaps, arbitrary stretched grid or generic boxes substituting for the focus presentation. |
| Politics | Distinct programmes for relevant parties/leaders, with internal choices. Outlooks and exact governing subparties are different things. |
| Gates | No extra 'over-focus' to unlock the already-ruling party. Avoid unnecessary date locks; retain genuine succession/event requirements. |
| Rewards | Calibrate values, costs, modifiers and reward bundles using comparable normal MD 2000-era focuses from Russia, Israel, Germany, Turkey and other relevant countries. Check units, duration and gates, then fit the target country and 1970 scenario. Rejected filler included 1% stability/10 PP or tiny construction gains as an entire programme. This preference does not authorize blanket numerical buffs. |
| Trade-offs | Both historically grounded exclusive options should be attractive enough that the player would like both. Give them distinct substantial benefits and a plausible modest drawback or opportunity cost. Audit the whole reachable programme and its stacking; strengthen existing choices before adding more. Shared ordinary development stays shared. Preserve serious historical starting problems rather than making every policy harmless. |
| Descriptions and effects | Learn and apply normal MD 2000-era conventions using suitable examples from Russia, Israel, Germany, Turkey and other relevant countries: specific national narrative and clear native effects with real values, costs and named outcomes. Reject raw design instructions, filler, placeholder localisation and developer bookkeeping in place of finished content. Review emitted prose and effects together; substantial rewrites receive an independent comparison. Word removal or a reference citation alone is insufficient. Hidden helpers need accurate previews. Duplicate graph-predecessor checks stay hidden; extra conditions remain visible. |
| Spirits | Relevant starting challenges, visible improvement and intentional party-bound cleanup. Avoid unconditional lists removing spirits a country never had. |
| Art | Inspect existing appropriate Cold War/MD icons. Texture existence is not semantic suitability. Show material art choices when requested. |
| Review | Economical agents for native MD comparison, inventory, layout and independent correctness. Give tasks meaningful names and inspect their findings. |
| Evidence | Static QA, rendered preview and engine test are different. Never call an observed hover crash fixed merely because unrelated warnings disappeared. |

## Failures to avoid

- Showing only additions, leaving neighbours out of the preview, then creating overlaps or vast empty zones.
- Preview and installed output using different coordinates, prerequisites, effects or generation sources.
- Treating a tooltip, localization entry, unconsumed variable or custom modifier registration as an executable benefit.
- Copying a state/equipment/subunit field into a country idea; confusing flat numbers, percentages, percentage points and tick frequency.
- Giving 'party support' to the wrong MD slot or pairing the wrong outlook with a subparty.
- Adding ceremony/unlock focuses despite the required party already governing.
- Copying another country's state IDs or leader/party/portrait references. Valid IDs can still point to the wrong geography after map changes.
- Inventing a new menu, fee, leadership system, virtual supply source or parallel EU system instead of integrating into existing MD systems.
- Replaying one-time rewards during refresh/load or retaining an old government's temporary programme without intent.
- Reporting catalogue totals as installed distinct people/assets or including held content as complete.

## Scoped examples

- **Spain:** user requested viable Falange/continuity and Bourbon alternatives, including economic/military continuation. Party programmes follow actual governing party; authoritarian entry has the relevant outlook gate. This is not every country's transition template.
- **Israel:** no Shia/Salafist paths were requested. User wanted genuine internal policy choices, office development, corrected Sinai geography and less generous easy integration rewards. Do not generalize its policy balance to other countries.
- **North Vietnam:** the user approved the visual concept before implementation, requested all focus cards to be clickable and a wider inspector, and then asked to retain the implementation lessons in these skills. The historical/alternate roster and January 1970 constraints remain Vietnam-specific; see `vietnam-integration.md`.
- **Soviet Union:** January 1970 constraints should be hard but manageable, with credible leader/party variation. Preserve Politburo/succession systems rather than replacing them with a new menu.
- **Greece/Cyprus:** programme funding and consent contracts are specific to their systems. A focus concerning another player's territory is not a shortcut around diplomacy or the recipient's response.

## Scenario boundaries

Initial research and starting armies/equipment were deferred, the 1985 start removed, and future research limited with specific exceptions. A focus task does not authorize rebuilding those starts, enabling deleted modules or reactivating archived chains. Recheck the current task and data before reusing old rewards.

Historical starting leaders stay unless explicitly changed. Additional politicians integrate with existing country systems. Current successor-list ordering is not a universal national-focus rule.

Resolve routine technical choices from actual MD analogues and existing approvals. Ask only when uncertainty changes gameplay, history, selected imagery or an approved design, giving a concrete understandable consequence. Do not re-ask permission for authorized work or quietly invent values for unresolved cases.

name: mdcw-modifier-audit
description: Audit modifier and effect mechanics in Millennium Dawn Cold War focus trees, including MD API support, calculation, visibility, stacking, cleanup, references, and 1970-scenario reachability. Use for focused-tree mechanic reviews; exclude general tree drafting and layout work.
---

# MD Cold War focus-tree mechanic audit

Use this skill to review whether a focus-tree reward has the intended, traceable effect in the current Millennium Dawn Cold War codebase. The audit is evidence-led: distinguish what source files prove from what requires an in-game test. Do not invent modifier keys, formulas, units, stacking rules, balance targets, or engine guarantees. Do not implement changes or add mechanics unless the user explicitly asks for implementation.

Start by locating the active MD Cold War repository and the installed MD source version. Treat the code anchors in the references as search starting points, not frozen truth; confirm their current contents and line numbers before relying on them. For a normal review:

An explicitly supplied fixture or review copy takes precedence over the live mod as the target. Missing external providers or consumers in an incomplete input are unresolved, not confirmed defects, unless the supplied provider universe is known to be complete. Do not broaden a bounded audit without need.

1. Trace each relevant focus from `available` and its prerequisite graph through `completion_reward`, referenced scripted effects/triggers, event options, ideas or dynamic modifiers, and their cleanup paths.
2. For every modifier or effect, establish its native MD form and scope. Trace a modifier into the actual system that reads or applies it; a matching word in a file, an icon, or an effect tooltip alone does not prove behavior.
3. When reviewing reward impact, compare both complete exclusive programmes, including follow-ups, cost, timing and meaningful drawbacks. The user wants two attractive, historically motivated alternatives rather than a strong option beside a punishment. Identify bureaucracy-only filler, duplicated small PP/stability rewards, bonuses discarded at a cap and nominally different choices delivering the same result. Check compatible whole-route stacking before proposing larger values; prefer distinct research/doctrine, assets, training or institutional outcomes over repeated generic combat buffs. Do not infer that all useful projects must be mutually exclusive or that every individual focus needs a malus.
4. Compare visible tooltips with executed effects. Verify values, units, duration, repeated grants, simultaneous sources, and intended removal, replacement or conditional deactivation on government/office changes. Separate permanent national gains from active leadership programmes.
5. Follow references transitively: event IDs and options, ideas, scripted effects and triggers, focus sprites and texture files, English localization keys, equipment types/design bonuses, research categories, and doctrine-cost categories.
6. Check that the route is reachable in the 1970 scenario from its real start setup, accounting for tree loading, starting government/party, date and country gates, event decisions, grouped prerequisites, exclusions and later-year formations. Multiple prerequisite blocks are AND; multiple focus fields inside a single block are OR.
7. Report concrete findings with source paths and current line anchors, the source evidence, the likely player-visible consequence, and any remaining runtime uncertainty. Separate confirmed defects from questions that need a live game check.

Review values, descriptions and effect presentation against mechanically comparable normal main MD 2000-era examples, including Russia, Israel, Germany and Turkey. Select relevant branches and trace their real providers/readers; record the country/focus, amount, unit, cost, duration and gates when using them as numerical benchmarks. Adapt magnitude to the target country and 1970 scenario without copying another country's history, state IDs or institutional design. Catch the demonstrated failures: raw design instructions or generic filler shipped as country narrative; internal invoice/queue documentation replacing a clear reward list; benefits, costs or spirit changes missing or misleading in the visible effects. Confirm country-specific meaning and native named/numeric presentation, including the actual current or frozen cost and a non-executing preview. A keyword blacklist, longer prose or a reference citation alone does not establish MD-quality presentation. For substantial rewrites, include an independent comparison of representative emitted descriptions and effects. Keep duplicate graph-predecessor checks hidden without concealing genuine extra conditions. Preserve the approved gameplay and distinguish source checks from observed native hovers.

Read [references/modifier-effect-audit.md](references/modifier-effect-audit.md) when verifying modifier keys, formulas, units, tooltips, stacking, dynamic ideas, equipment, research, or doctrine effects. Read [references/focus-graph-and-scenario.md](references/focus-graph-and-scenario.md) when auditing transitive references, party-change cleanup, or 1970-scenario reachability.

For funding/retry contracts, recipient-owned offers, construction feasibility, crisis observers or leader expiry, read [transaction-boundaries.md](references/transaction-boundaries.md). Its focused source/test examples do not establish engine behavior.

For generated trees, trace the reviewed focuses and their applicable overrides through staged output into loaded files. Keep coverage within the requested scope unless findings justify expanding it. The references contain Soviet patterns for dynamic rewards, programme ownership, recipient-controlled agreements and joint-focus scopes, not a certificate that the entire Soviet tree passed a game test.

Static parsers, source searches, and local validators can establish source consistency and graph properties; they do not prove that HOI4 loads the tree, renders the exact tooltip, evaluates every scope as intended, or preserves behavior in a save. State those limits plainly. Do not convert audit work into a balance redesign or broad code cleanup.
